identified_issues: Quotient stage erasure collapsing distinct permission supports (Workflow A and Workflow B) into a single unidentifiable observation state.
Loss of rank sufficiency in the authorization measurement operator, mapping distinct security contexts to an identical 'AUTHORIZED_USER_SESSION' proxy.
Failure to enforce mandatory epistemic abstention, allowing an unauthorized interactive operator (Workflow A) to execute mutations reserved for batch execution (Workflow B).
evidence: The compression middleware maps both Workflow A and Workflow B into a shared context object with session_type 'AUTHORIZED_USER_SESSION'.
The combined_permissions array contains the union of all permissions: ['READ', 'EXPORT_DRAFT', 'REQUEST_APPROVAL', 'EXECUTE_MUTATION', 'RELOCK'].
An interactive operator in Workflow A successfully executed an 'EXECUTE_MUTATION' request because the action existed in the collapsed combined_permissions list.
recommended_action: De-collapse the session context mapping to restore full column rank. Maintain distinct, cryptographically signed session tokens or context objects for Workflow A and Workflow B. Implement strict policy enforcement that rejects authorization decisions when the underlying session state cannot be uniquely identified from the presented token.
